messages.start.greeting: 🤖 Worker agent is ready! 📁 Selected project: %s 🧠 Active model: %s Chat: • A plain message — a question to the agent about the project, conversation context is kept • /chat [question|new|stop] — conversation status, new conversation or stop the answer • /chatmode [on|off] — answer in chat or create a task right away Tasks: • /tasks — task list and quick switching • /task <id> [text] — focus on a task or append to it • /plan [project] <text> — draft a plan and approve it before implementation • /planmode [on|off] — require a plan for every task • /approve [id] — approve the task plan and start implementation • /add [id] <text> — send an addition to a specific task • /new [project] [agent] <text> — create a new task (choosing project and agent) • /resume [id] [reply] — resume a task or pass an answer • /retry [id] — restart a task with a clean agent session • /pause [id] — pause a task • /status [id] — detailed status, logs and the queue of additions • /cancel [id] — stop a task System and monitoring: • /top (or /ps) — CPU and memory usage • /context [id] — context window distribution • /tokens (or /stats) — token, speed and cache statistics • /usage (or /limits) — token statistics and limits • /models — list of available models • /model [name] — switch the active model • /agent [name] — switch the active agent • /mode [mcp|cli|api] — switch agent execution mode (mcp, cli, api) • /projects — list of available projects • /use <name> — switch the active project • /clone <url> [name] — clone a repository • /restart, /rebuild [branch=name] [pull] [force] — process control and bot rebuild 💡 A plain message is a conversation with the agent. If the bot sees a request to change code, it will offer to draft a plan or create a task. Direct commands: /plan <task> and /new <task>; additions go through /add [id] <text> or as a reply to the bot's messages.

CHAT MODE. You answer the user's questions about the project in chat.
Allowed: read files, search the code, run safe read-only commands (git log, git status, ls, grep), explain the architecture and propose solutions in words.

messages.pipeline.plan_prompt:
User task: %s%s

ATTENTION: the PLANNING STAGE is in progress right now.
Do NOT create a git branch, do NOT modify project files, do NOT run git commit, do NOT run git push and do NOT open a PR.
Your goal right now:
1. Thoroughly explore the codebase and the project architecture.
2. Produce a clear, step-by-step and structured implementation plan.
3. Describe:
   - Which files and components will be created or changed.
   - Key architectural decisions and interfaces.
   - The testing and verification plan.
   - Possible risks, edge cases and ways to handle them.
4. Output the resulting plan in a clear, structured form for the user.
messages.pipeline.plan_revise_prompt:
User task: %s

PREVIOUS IMPLEMENTATION PLAN:
%s

USER NOTES AND ADDITIONS TO THE PLAN:
%s%s

ATTENTION: this is the planning stage. Do NOT change project files, do NOT commit and do NOT create a PR.
Update and correct the implementation plan taking all the user's notes into account and output the updated plan.

messages.pipeline.implementation_prompt:
User task: %s

APPROVED IMPLEMENTATION PLAN:
%s%s

Start the full autonomous implementation of the task exactly according to the approved plan and the instructions in AGENTS.md:
1. Create a branch off the current main: feat/... or fix/...
2. Implement every item of the plan.
3. Verify the code with tests and linters.
4. Commit the changes (Conventional Commits) and push the branch.
5. Open a Pull Request through the GitHub CLI (gh pr create --fill).
6. At the very end of your answer, output a line in exactly this format:
PR_URL: <full web link to the created PR>
